candidate: disabled structured handoff fence + CAS-bound Manager postcondition receipt + canonical whole protected-state digest + deterministic replacement-reset mint gate + exact durable backlog insertion + current-state reconcile/rearm
audit_scope: Source-derived Argus recovery adaptation only. This audit tests whether the current public Argus implementation really contains the failure seams and primitives the proposal relies on, and whether the proposed end-to-end repair already exists or has been independently reproduced. It does not claim that the adaptation has been implemented in Argus or O.

official_release_mirror.note: Same project/release lineage, not an independent implementation or independent reproduction.

grade.proposed_full_recovery_implementation: C / not present in inspected public Argus

findings.finding: The precommit/replace split is a real, officially regression-tested failure mode.
findings.evidence: Argus compare_and_swap_continuous_config executes before_write while holding the continuous lock and before replacing continuous.json. tests/daemon/test_state_portable.py::test_replace_failure_after_callback_surfaces_instead_of_false deterministically commits a side effect, forces the continuous replace to fail, observes ContinuousConfigCommitError, and verifies the old ContinuousConfigState remains while the side effect survives.

findings.finding: The production Manager continuous handoff uses exactly that split-prone ordering.
findings.evidence: manager/front_door.py::manager_continuous_handoff passes _commit as before_write. _commit performs PreparedManagerHandoff.commit(), replacement backlog supersession, and optional persist before continuous.json replacement. manager/dispatch.py supplies a persist callback that creates the operator-priority BacklogItem and appends it with Backlog.add. Therefore a continuous replace failure can leave Manager/backlog side effects durable while continuous state is still the predecessor generation.

findings.finding: The worker is correct that an ad-hoc handoff_fence field would currently be lost.
findings.evidence: daemon/state.py::ContinuousConfigState contains only enabled, objective, open_ended, done_reason, done_at, generation. _read_continuous_state_unlocked reconstructs only those fields; _continuous_state_reserve_text and _write_continuous_config_unlocked serialize only them; _same_continuous_state compares only them. No handoff_fence or ManagerReconcileReceiptV1 symbol exists in the inspected public preview source. A first-class schema extension is therefore required rather than injecting an unknown JSON key.

findings.finding: The proposed replacement-reset mint checks are source-aligned, including the important same-stage case.
findings.evidence: skills/stage_machine.py::reset_stage_for_replacement_intent calls _set_stage(direction='reset', downgrade_downstream=True, legacy_rollback_history=True). _set_stage allows reset onto the same current stage, forces the target to in_progress, downgrades downstream done/ready/in_progress/skipped to pending, and appends both stage_history and rollback_history. vertical_select.reset_stage_for_new_intent is fail-open on ValueError, so a receipt mint gate must explicitly require the reset postconditions rather than trusting its boolean path implicitly.

findings.finding: Canonical hashing of the parsed whole PIPELINE_STATE object is technically well motivated, but it is a reconciliation detector, not a durability proof for PIPELINE_STATE itself.
findings.evidence: core/pipeline_state.py writes the full heterogeneous JSON object with sort_keys=True through a sibling temporary and os.replace, but does not fsync the file or parent directory. A canonical parsed-object SHA-256 avoids whitespace/key-order noise and covers stage/policy/history fields omitted by a route-only digest. If the stronger receipt survives a power loss while the weaker pipeline write does not, digest mismatch can force Manager reconciliation; this still requires the receipt/fence implementation and recovery test to exist.

findings.finding: The proposed exact durable Backlog insertion is not an existing Argus primitive and is the largest concrete implementation gap.
findings.evidence: life/memory.py::Backlog.add appends without checking an existing item id. add_many rejects duplicate ids by raising rather than returning an existing row idempotently. The production continuous persist callback uses Backlog.add with root_task_id, so retrying after the split can append a second row with the same id. _atomic_rewrite_jsonl uses os.replace but no file/parent-directory fsync. Generic Backlog.update sets any existing attribute, so id and ts are not immutable identities. The proposed (existing, inserted=False) retry contract plus immutable creation_stamp and power-loss durability therefore require new code and tests.

findings.finding: No end-to-end public implementation or matched independent reproduction of clean-os-g1-005 was found.
findings.evidence: The inspected public Argus main has no handoff_fence or ManagerReconcileReceiptV1 implementation and no source-exact second-replace regression that performs disabled fence -> Manager reset -> receipt attach -> exact backlog insert -> forced final enable failure -> reconcile/rearm. Public web/GitHub searches surfaced the Argus repositories but no independent implementation/reproduction of this recovery sequence.

safe_conclusion: clean-os-g1-005 is strongly grounded in a real Argus crash-consistency defect and mostly accurate about the schema/reset primitives it would need. It should not yet be treated as a validated recovery solution. The public implementation still lacks the first-class fence/receipt schema, idempotent power-loss-durable backlog insertion, and the full second-replace crash/rearm regression. The strongest new audit result is that backlog retry safety is weaker than the proposal's target contract: current Backlog.add can duplicate the exact root_task_id and current backlog persistence is not fsync-complete.
reopen_or_promotion_conditions: A public Argus change adds handoff_fence/ManagerReconcileReceipt as first-class ContinuousConfigState fields with read/write/reserve/_same/CAS coverage and backward-compatible old-state reads.

A backlog primitive provides exact-id idempotent insertion returning existing/inserted status, protects immutable creation identity, and has file + parent-directory durability semantics appropriate to the claimed power-loss model.

A deterministic regression executes the complete replacement sequence and forces the final continuous enable replace/durability failure after Manager state + receipt + backlog insertion, then proves one physical backlog identity and exact rearm without rerunning stale work.
An independent implementation or protocol-matched fault-injection reproduction appears.
exact_next_action: Do not repeat unchanged clean-os-g1-005. On the next bootstrap-valid invocation, select a different source-qualified non-evaluation C19-or-later candidate unless one of the reopen/promotion conditions above is newly satisfied.
